templates.title: Review gate
templates.summary: A builder works, an isolated critic checks the change against a written checklist, failures loop back, and a human approves the merge.

doc.name: Review gate
doc.goal: {{task}} Done when every item in {{checklist}} is shown to hold, `{{test-command}}` passes, and a human approves the merge.

template.title: Review gate
template.summary: A builder works, an isolated critic checks the change against a written checklist, failures loop back, and a human approves the merge.
template.whenToUse: Work, then a separate reviewer, then iterate or pass: the change needs a second pair of eyes against a checklist that already exists.
template.notFor: Work where the tests alone decide done (use grind-loop), or where nobody has written down what good means yet (use spec-then-loop).

slots.ask: What should be built or changed? One or two sentences a builder can act on.
slots.example: Add a slugify(text) function to src/strings.ts that lowercases, strips accents and joins words with single hyphens.

slots.ask: Which command runs the tests?
Which file holds the checklist the critic judges against?

doc.description: A builder implements the task. A critic in a fresh context checks the diff and test output against a written checklist; failures return to the builder with REVIEW.md, and a pass goes to a human merge gate, whose rejection also returns to the builder. The loop stops when the bar passes, at its round cap, or at its dispatch budget. Builder and critic share a tier, which the validator flags; heterogeneous-critic is the same shape with the critic on another tier.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.brief: Do the task in the code, with tests. On a later round, read REVIEW.md first and address each finding, or say why it does not apply. Run the test command before you report, and do not review your own work beyond that.
outputs: CHANGES.md: what changed this round and which findings it addresses

nodes.name: Critic
nodes.brief: Judge the change against the checklist, one line per item, citing the file and line that satisfies it or saying it is unmet; use the repository only to understand what the change touches. Run the test command yourself rather than trusting a report; you judge, you do not fix. Verdict pass only when every item holds and the tests pass; invalid-evidence when the diff or checklist cannot be read.
inputs: the repository as the change leaves it, read-only
outputs: REVIEW.md: one line per checklist item and a verdict line

nodes.name: Merge approval
nodes.prompt: The critic passed the change against the checklist. Merge it?

evidence: the repository as the change leaves it, read-only

bar.name: Review checklist
bar.acceptance: Every checklist item is cited as satisfied with a file and line, and `{{test-command}}` exits 0.

templates.title: Grind loop
templates.summary: A fast builder works against the test suite until it passes, bounded by rounds and minutes.

doc.name: Grind loop

template.title: Grind loop
template.summary: A fast builder works against the test suite until it passes, bounded by rounds and minutes.
template.whenToUse: Done and good are the same: tests, types or a task list supply the back pressure, so a passing check is the finish line.
template.notFor: Work where passing tests is not the same as good (taste, design, prose); use review-gate or taste-polish there.

slots.ask: What should be built or changed? One or two sentences a builder can act on.
slots.example: Add a slugify(text) function to src/strings.ts that lowercases, strips accents and joins words with single hyphens.

slots.ask: Which command runs the tests?

doc.description: A builder changes the code and a check runs the tests. A failure goes back to the builder with the test output; a pass ends the run. The check is the bar, so there is no critic. The loop stops at its round cap or its time budget if the tests never pass.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.brief: Make the task true by changing the code, adding tests where they are missing. Do not skip, weaken or delete a test to get a pass. On a later round, start from the failing output you are handed. Report what you changed and which tests now pass.
outputs: CHANGES.md: what changed this round and why

check.pass: exit code 0 and no test skipped

templates.title: Ralph loop
templates.summary: A fresh builder takes the top unchecked item of a plan file each round, commits on green and appends what it learned to an agent file, until the plan is empty.

doc.name: Ralph loop
doc.goal: {{task}} Done when every item in {{plan-file}} is marked done and `{{test-command}}` passes.

template.title: Ralph loop
template.summary: A fresh builder takes the top unchecked item of a plan file each round, commits on green and appends what it learned to an agent file, until the plan is empty.
template.whenToUse: The work is already a prioritized list of small items that tests can check one at a time, and you want a fresh context per item with the plan and an agent file as the only memory.
template.notFor: One item that needs judgment rather than a test (use review-gate or taste-polish), or a plan whose items are too large or too coupled to finish one at a time.

slots.ask: What is the work as a whole, in one or two sentences? The plan file holds the items.
slots.example: Build the text-statistics module the plan describes, one item at a time.

slots.ask: Which file holds the plan: a Markdown checklist, top item first, `- [ ]` open and `- [x]` done?
Which file holds the operating notes the builder reads first and may append learnings to?
Which command runs the tests?

credits.name: Geoffrey Huntley's ralph loop
credits.note: one prompt piped into a fresh session per pass; one item of work per pass from a plan file; state on disk; the human as the brake, here replaced by stops

doc.description: The plan file is the unit of work. Each round a fresh builder takes the top unchecked item, makes it true, runs the tests, and on green marks it done, commits and appends what it learned to the agent file. A test check catches an item that broke something; a plan check sends the builder back for the next item while any remains. The loop stops when the plan is empty, when the same failure repeats, at its round cap or at its dispatch budget: the stops the original loop leaves to the human.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.brief: Read {{agent-file}} first, then take only the top unchecked item of {{plan-file}}: make it true in the code with tests, run `{{test-command}}`, and on green mark the item done, append what you learned to {{agent-file}} and commit. Never start a second item, and never skip, weaken or delete a test to get a pass. On a later round, start from the failing output you are handed, which may come from the item you just marked done. Report the item you took, what changed and whether the tests passed.
outputs: the change for the item, with tests

check.pass: exit code 0 and no test skipped

nodes.name: Plan empty?
nodes.description: Counts the unchecked items left in the plan. grep prints the count and exits 1 when it is zero, so the printed count is the result, not the exit code.

check.pass: the printed count is 0: no unchecked item remains in {{plan-file}}

templates.title: Red-team loop
templates.summary: A separate attacker records reproducible failing traces; the builder is given only the traces, until no new one appears.

doc.name: Red-team loop
doc.goal: {{task}} Done when a red team attacking {{attack-surface}} stops finding new failing traces.

template.title: Red-team loop
template.summary: A separate attacker records reproducible failing traces; the builder is given only the traces, until no new one appears.
template.whenToUse: A separate attacker should produce failing traces and the builder should see only those: hardening against inputs or abuse nobody has listed yet.
template.notFor: Work with a known list of cases to satisfy (use grind-loop against tests), or judging quality rather than breaking things.

slots.ask: What should be built or changed? One or two sentences a builder can act on.
slots.example: Harden login and session handling in src/auth/ against malformed input, replayed tokens and timing leaks.

slots.ask: Which command runs the tests?
What should the red team attack?
slots.example: the login endpoint and session handling in src/auth/

doc.description: A builder hardens the code; a frontier red team in a fresh context attacks the stated surface and writes each reproducible failure as a trace in traces/, which it alone owns. The builder sees only the traces, not the attacker's reasoning. The loop ends when an attack round finds nothing, stops when rounds stop bringing a new failing trace, and is capped by rounds and dispatches.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.brief: Make the task hold under attack. Each round you see only the failing traces in traces/: make each one pass without special-casing it, and add it to the test suite. Keep `{{test-command}}` green and report which traces now pass.
outputs: the change, with a test per fixed trace

nodes.name: Red team
nodes.brief: Attack {{attack-surface}} and record each failure you can reproduce as a trace in traces/: the input, how to run it, and the wrong result. Traces are all the builder sees, so each must reproduce on its own. You attack; you do not fix. Verdict fail when you have a new failing trace, pass when you found none.
outputs: traces/: one reproducible failing trace per file
ATTACK.md: what was attacked and how, written whether or not a trace was found

bar.name: No new failing trace
bar.acceptance: A full attack round finds no failing trace, and every recorded trace passes in `{{test-command}}`.

templates.title: Spec then loop
templates.summary: A planner writes the answer key, a human approves it, then a builder and an isolated critic loop against it.

doc.name: Spec then loop
doc.goal: {{task}} Done when every line of an approved ACCEPTANCE.md is shown to hold and `{{test-command}}` passes.

template.title: Spec then loop
template.summary: A planner writes the answer key, a human approves it, then a builder and an isolated critic loop against it.
template.whenToUse: No external reference product exists: a planning pass writes an answer key (ACCEPTANCE.md) that becomes the bar. The default for zero-to-one work.
template.notFor: Work with a reference or checklist already in hand (use review-gate or taste-polish), or changes so small that writing acceptance criteria costs more than the change.

slots.ask: What should be built or changed? One or two sentences a builder can act on.
slots.example: Add CSV export to the reports page: a download button that exports the rows currently shown.

slots.ask: Which command runs the tests?

credits.name: Answer-key-first Gauntlet, a community modification of Matt Pocock's Wayfinder
credits.note: write the spec and a pass/fail answer key before the loop; the modification is known from a secondary write-up, not a primary source

doc.description: A frontier planner turns the task into ACCEPTANCE.md, a short list of observable behaviors. A human approves it; rejecting ends the run so the task can be restated. A builder then works and a critic in a fresh context judges the change line by line against the approved file, which is the loop's bar. The loop stops when every line holds, at its round cap, or at its dispatch budget.

nodes.name: Planner
nodes.brief: Turn the task into ACCEPTANCE.md: the observable behaviors that would make it done, each checkable by reading code or running `{{test-command}}`. Name what is out of scope. Keep it short enough to review in a minute, and write no code.

nodes.name: Approve the spec
nodes.prompt: Is ACCEPTANCE.md the right definition of done? Rejecting ends the run so the task can be restated.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.brief: Do the task until every line of ACCEPTANCE.md holds. The acceptance file is fixed: if a line is wrong, say so in your report rather than working around it. Run `{{test-command}}` before you report; on a later round, start from REVIEW.md.

nodes.name: Critic
nodes.brief: Judge the change against ACCEPTANCE.md line by line, citing the file and line or the test that shows each one holds; use the repository only to understand what the change touches. Run `{{test-command}}` yourself. You judge; you do not fix, and you do not edit the acceptance file. Verdict pass only when every line holds; invalid-evidence when the diff or the file cannot be read.
inputs: the repository as the change leaves it, read-only
outputs: REVIEW.md: one line per acceptance item and a verdict line

evidence: the repository as the change leaves it, read-only

bar.name: ACCEPTANCE.md
bar.acceptance: Every line of ACCEPTANCE.md is shown to hold, and `{{test-command}}` exits 0.

templates.title: Debate then build
templates.summary: Two planners argue opposite approaches for a capped number of rounds, a judge writes the plan, a human approves it, and a small grind loop builds it.

doc.name: Debate then build
doc.goal: {{task}} Done when a judged plan is approved by a human and its first version passes `{{test-command}}`.

template.title: Debate then build
template.summary: Two planners argue opposite approaches for a capped number of rounds, a judge writes the plan, a human approves it, and a small grind loop builds it.
template.whenToUse: Short adversarial planning, then a small build graph: the right approach is genuinely unclear and a wrong choice is expensive to undo.
template.notFor: Work with an obvious approach, or where drafts are cheaper than arguments (use tournament-then-judge).

slots.ask: What should be built or changed? One or two sentences a builder can act on.
slots.example: Choose and build a caching approach for the slow /search endpoint in src/api/search.ts.

slots.ask: Which command runs the tests?

doc.description: One planner argues for the simplest approach that could work, the other against it and for the strongest alternative. A frontier judge reads both cases and either asks for one more exchange or writes PLAN.md; the debate has a round cap, after which the judge must decide. A human approves the plan, and a fast builder grinds the first version against the tests.

nodes.name: Planner A
nodes.brief: Argue for the simplest approach that could do the task, and answer the other side's strongest point when there is one. Keep your case under a page in CASE-A.md and concede the risks that are real. Write no code.

nodes.name: Planner B
nodes.brief: Argue against the approach in CASE-A.md and for the strongest alternative, answering its best points directly. Keep your case under a page in CASE-B.md and concede the risks that are real. Write no code.

nodes.name: Judge
nodes.brief: Read both cases. If one more exchange would change your choice, emit verdict rebut and write REBUT.md naming the point each side must answer; otherwise, or when the debate is out of rounds, write PLAN.md with the approach, why it won, and the smallest first version with its checks, and emit pass. You decide; you write no code.
outputs: PLAN.md, or REBUT.md when asking for another round

nodes.name: Approve the plan
nodes.prompt: Build the first version PLAN.md describes?

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.brief: Build the first version PLAN.md describes and nothing past it, with tests. On a later round, start from the failing output you are handed. Report what you built and anything in the plan that proved wrong.

check.pass: exit code 0 and no test skipped

bar.name: Both cases answered
bar.acceptance: Each case answers the other's strongest point, and the judge has written PLAN.md.

templates.title: Tournament then judge
templates.summary: Three fast candidates build in parallel, a cheap check drops the broken ones, a frontier judge picks one finalist, and a builder finishes it.

doc.name: Tournament then judge
doc.goal: {{task}} Done when the finalist the judge picks is finished and `{{test-command}}` passes.

template.title: Tournament then judge
template.summary: Three fast candidates build in parallel, a cheap check drops the broken ones, a frontier judge picks one finalist, and a builder finishes it.
template.whenToUse: Cheap candidates, then spend the expensive critic on finalists: the approach is open, drafts are cheap, and comparing working options beats arguing about them.
template.notFor: Work with one obvious approach, or coupled changes to a shared core: candidates that must touch the same files cannot run side by side.

slots.ask: What should be built or changed? One or two sentences a builder can act on.
slots.example: Add a slugify(text) function to src/strings.ts that lowercases, strips accents and joins words with single hyphens.

slots.ask: Which command runs the tests?
What should the judge prefer among candidates that all pass the tests?
slots.example: The smallest change that reads clearly and handles empty and non-ASCII input.

doc.description: Three fast builders each draft the whole task in their own folder, in parallel. A check runs the tests on each and keeps the ones that pass. A frontier judge sees only those finalists and picks one against the stated criteria, naming any idea worth borrowing from the others. A builder finishes the winner. No loop: the tournament runs once.

nodes.name: Candidate A
nodes.brief: Build your own complete take on the task inside candidates/a/ and nowhere else. A runnable draft beats a polished fragment, and an approach different from the obvious one is welcome. Report your approach in one paragraph.

nodes.name: Candidate B
nodes.brief: Build your own complete take on the task inside candidates/b/ and nowhere else. A runnable draft beats a polished fragment, and an approach different from the obvious one is welcome. Report your approach in one paragraph.

nodes.name: Candidate C
nodes.brief: Build your own complete take on the task inside candidates/c/ and nowhere else. A runnable draft beats a polished fragment, and an approach different from the obvious one is welcome. Report your approach in one paragraph.

nodes.name: Finalist filter
nodes.description: Runs once, after all three candidates are in.

check.pass: at least one candidate passes; those that pass are the finalists

nodes.name: Judge
nodes.brief: Pick the one finalist to finish, judging against {{criteria}}; you see only the candidates that passed the filter. Write PICK.md naming the winner, why, and the best idea worth borrowing from another finalist. You pick; you do not edit any candidate.
outputs: PICK.md: the winner, the reason, one idea to borrow

nodes.name: Finisher
nodes.brief: Finish the candidate PICK.md names: move it into its real place, close its gaps, and fold in the borrowed idea if it fits. Leave the other candidates untouched. Run `{{test-command}}` before you report.

template.title: Human-gated irreversible step
template.summary: A human gate, then the one node that performs an irreversible action, then a stop: insert it before any merge, publish, spend or delete.
template.whenToUse: A step cannot be undone (merge, spend, publish, delete) and must wait for a human decision; this fragment satisfies E_IRREVERSIBLE_NO_GATE.
template.notFor: Reversible steps, where a gate only slows the run; and it gates only the way in you connect to it: every edge into the action must pass the gate.

outputs: ACTION.md: what was done and its result
